subject: Discovery: FluxPay tool/function calling & structured-output requirements
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fluxpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T14:05:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps (tool-calls + structured output)

Jordan / Priya — thanks for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. I kept the summary terse and called out the structured-output needs we discussed.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Reconciliation automation is failing at scale: current rule-based matchers miss ~6–8% of payments, creating manual review overhead.
- Incorrect/missing metadata from downstream providers (PO number, original_payment_id).
- Latency in downstream lookups (3rd-party ledger) means your current LLM-based enrichment causes timeouts.

Goals / success criteria:
- Achieve >=95% automated reconciliation accuracy for ISO-20022-style records.
- Reduce manual review queue by 60% within Q4.
- Structured outputs (deterministic JSON for downstream jobs) with stable keys and validation schema.

Current stack you described:
- Ingest: S3 -> Kafka -> internal enrichment
- Enrichment: LLM inference running on a mix of managed endpoints + on-prem GPU hosts
- Orchestration: Airflow for batch; synchronous REST for customer-facing calls

Structured-output & tool/function calling requirements we discussed:
- Single-shot deterministic JSON response that the downstream worker can parse without heuristics.
- Function-call style responses are preferred: explicit "action" object with action_name and args, where args is a strict JSON object matching a schema.
- Example required fields: {invoice_id, original_payment_id, matched_amount_cents, match_confidence, action_recommendation} — match_confidence numeric 0.0-1.0.
- When calling external ledger lookups, the model should return a list of ledger_ids (array) or an explicit "defer_to_tool" action so your service can run the lookup synchronously.
- Deterministic formatting is critical: stable key ordering is helpful but more important is strict types (strings, ints, booleans) and no human prose mixed in the response fields.

Attachments: I attached the raw discovery notes and a small example schema (fluxpay-example-schema.json) with a compact contract you can drop into validation.

Open/questions / risks:
- Latency SLO: you mentioned a 400ms p90 target for customer-facing enrichment. For some of the synchronous ledger calls that may require fallback policies (cached results or async enrichment + webhook).
- Scoped data residency & audit: if we need private deployment (VPC), we should flag that early — Redwood Private supports this, but procurement lead times differ.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Review the attached example schema and flag any required fields or type disagreements (due 2026-07-23).
2) Technical deep-dive with one of our inference engineers (Marcus Lin) and Marissa on 2026-07-28 to validate latency profiles and demo function-calling behavior.
3) If schema checks out, we provide a short PoC plan: 2-week sandbox using a sample of your failed reconciliation cases.

If that matches your view, Jordan — please confirm the 7/28 window and whether you want the PoC scoped to sync REST calls or batch enrichment first.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- discovery-notes.pdf (summary highlights, redacted)
- fluxpay-example-schema.json (JSON schema stub)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fluxpay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@fluxpay.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps (tool-calls + structured output)

Thanks Grace — this is a great summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we route the schema internally:

1) For the case where the model returns ledger_ids, do you expect Redwood to call our ledger tool directly (we expose an internal REST endpoint) or is the preferred pattern for the model to emit an action that our service executes?
2) On latency: the 400ms p90 is a hard-ish target for customer-facing flows. For batch reconciliations we can tolerate longer. Can you call out which parts of your proposed PoC would be synchronous vs async?

Also — could you include an example where the model returns multiple candidate invoice IDs with confidence scores? That will help us feel comfortable about blindly accepting automated matches.

I can confirm availability for 7/28; we need to confirm who from our side will join (I expect one engineer + product).

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Integrations | FluxPay
jordan.lee@fluxpay.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fluxpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps (tool-calls + structured output)

Jordan — great questions. Short answers up front, then a compact example you can paste into validation.

1) Pattern: we recommend the model emit an explicit action object (function-call pattern). That keeps control in your service and avoids having the model access internal endpoints directly. Typical flow: model -> action: {"defer_to_tool": true, "tool": "ledger_lookup", "args": {"candidate_keys": [...] } } -> your service executes ledger_lookup -> returns results -> model finalizes structured output. This gives you traceability and audit.

2) PoC sync vs async:
- Customer-facing enrichment: synchronous path with an aggressive timeout and fallback to a cached or "defer" action.
- Backfill/batch reconciliation: asynchronous, we can run larger-context models and follow-up passes.

Attached is a minimal example output (also in fluxpay-example-schema.json). Note the model is asked to return a single well-typed JSON blob with an action array for tool calls if needed.

Example (compact):
{
  "action": "finalize_match",
  "result": {
    "invoice_id": "INV-2026-000123",
    "original_payment_id": "PAY-7890",
    "matched_amount_cents": 102500,
    "match_confidence": 0.96,
    "candidates": [
      {"invoice_id": "INV-2026-000123", "confidence": 0.96},
      {"invoice_id": "INV-2026-000124", "confidence": 0.03}
    ],
    "tool_actions": [
      {"action_name": "ledger_lookup", "args": {"ledger_keys": ["LGR-12345", "LGR-67890"]} }
    ]
  }
}

Notes on deterministic formatting: please validate types strictly (e.g., match_confidence numeric, not string). We recommend validating against the attached JSON Schema before consuming.

Next steps I suggest:
- Jordan: confirm who from your eng/product will join 7/28 (we recommend an eng + product).
- Marissa/Ben: I proposed Marcus on the call to talk kernels/latency tradeoffs and to sketch an initial batching/caching profile.
- Jordan: if you can return any sample failed-case rows ahead of the call, we can pre-run them through the PoC harness and show concrete before/after.

I'll update the HubSpot deal with the meeting once we lock the attendee list.

Thanks,
Grace

Attachments included: fluxpay-example-schema.json (same compact schema as above)
